Green Bean Casserole

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Green Bean Casserole is a classic American side dish traditionally served at Thanksgiving. It combines tender green beans with a creamy mushroom sauce and a crispy fried onion topping, making it a comforting staple on holiday tables.

Ingredients

  • 2 (14.5 oz / 411 g) cans of cut green beans, drained
  • 1 (10.5 oz / 298 g) can of condensed cream of mushroom soup
  • 3/4 cup (180 ml) milk
  • 1/8 tsp black pepper
  • 1 tsp soy sauce
  • 1 1/3 cups (100 g) French fried onions, divided

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine the cream of mushroom soup, milk, black pepper, and soy sauce until smooth.
  3. Add the drained green beans and 2/3 cup (about 67 g) of the French fried onions to the bowl and gently mix.
  4. Transfer the mixture to a 1 1/2-quart (1.4 L) casserole dish and spread evenly.
  5. Bake uncovered for 25 minutes or until hot and bubbling.
  6. Sprinkle the remaining 2/3 cup (about 33 g) of French fried onions evenly over the top.
  7. Return to the oven and bake for an additional 5 minutes or until the onions are golden brown.

Tips

  • Use fresh or frozen green beans if preferred; blanch fresh beans before using.
  • For a richer flavor, sauté mushrooms and onions to add to the sauce.
  • Make the casserole a few hours ahead and refrigerate; add crispy onions and bake just before serving.
